paras: The Snyder hotel crowd of 1903 was an incident in Snyder, reported in late June 1903, in which a crowd went to a hotel to demand a Black man who had come to town as a traveling man's packer. The man was not found, and the only report described the town as determined to let no Black person remain there.
According to the Guthrie Daily Leader, Snyder "wants no negroes within its limits." The report names neither the town's county nor its state, though it appeared in a Guthrie, Oklahoma paper.

Shortly before 30 June 1903, an unnamed traveling man arrived in Snyder with a Black man, whom the paper called a "Senegambian," employed as his packer. Word of the man's presence soon spread through the town. A crowd then gathered and went to the hotel, demanding that the man be handed over. He was not found, and the report does not say what became of him or of the traveling man.
The paper closed by noting a "determination to permit no member of the black race to remain there." No arrests, official response or further incidents appear in the coverage.

The episode is known from a single paragraph on the front page of the Guthrie Daily Leader of 30 June 1903. The item was written as a matter-of-fact news note, opening with the town's wish to exclude Black people and using the term "Senegambian" for the man, with no comment on the crowd's conduct. No other white paper and no Black paper was found to have reported the incident.
